SAS DATEJUL(julian-date)

Source: R/doc_functions.R
sas_f_datejul.Rd

SAS date from a Julian date (yyddd or yyyyddd). See the SAS documentation (Functions and CALL Routines).

Arguments

j

Julian date as a number yyddd or yyyyddd (year followed by the 3-digit day of the year); a 2-digit year is resolved with the YEARCUTOFF option. Missing gives missing.

Value

A vector with one result per element (arguments are recycled), as the SAS function returns per observation.

Differences from R

SAS dates count days and SAS datetimes count seconds from 1960-01-01; R's Date and POSIXct start at 1970-01-01.

See also

Other datetime functions: sas_f_datdif(), sas_f_date(), sas_f_datepart(), sas_f_datetime(), sas_f_day(), sas_f_dhms(), sas_f_hms(), sas_f_hour(), sas_f_intck(), sas_f_intnx(), sas_f_juldate(), sas_f_juldate7(), sas_f_mdy(), sas_f_minute(), sas_f_month(), sas_f_qtr(), sas_f_second(), sas_f_time(), sas_f_timepart(), sas_f_today(), sas_f_week(), sas_f_weekday(), sas_f_year(), sas_f_yrdif()

Examples

# DATEJUL: each call is explained above it and followed by its result

# DATEJUL converts a Julian date yyyyddd (day 75 of 2024) to a SAS date value:
# 15 March 2024 is 23450.
sas_f_datejul(2024075)  # datejul(2024075) = 23450
#> [1] 23450

# Day 1 of 2024 is 1 January 2024, SAS date 23376.
sas_f_datejul(2024001)  # datejul(2024001) = 23376
#> [1] 23376

# 1 January 1960 is SAS date 0, the origin of SAS dates.
sas_f_datejul(1960001)  # datejul(1960001) = 0
#> [1] 0

# A missing argument gives a missing result.
sas_f_datejul(NA_real_)  # datejul(.) = .
#> [1] NA
